$Comment: The Disenchanting Table's ritual, a standalone action both tables Ref (Stations/Disenchanting_Table.json as is, Stations/Disenchanting_Table_Greater.json through its child action Disenchant_Greater). One piece of gear goes on the table and comes apart over six beats; what it gives back is whatever the vanilla Salvage bench would give for it, and the table's own payout is layered on top through Bonus. Recipe.FromCrafting derives one conversion per vanilla salvage recipe, full outputs at native quantities, so a third-party piece that ships its own salvage recipe is covered with nothing written here. Fallback takes the gear no salvage recipe names: a share of the piece's own crafting recipe when it has one, otherwise the piece is consumed for the Bonus rolls alone (the essence-only route). Fallback.Input scopes both routes to weapons, armor, tools and utility gear (backpacks, the quiver, the helipack) by Type tag (shields are Type Weapon in vanilla). A piece meets three checks as it is placed, before any salvage row or route sees it. First the things that must never go on the table: the non-gear by the protect-list file ProtectLists/Disenchanting_Tables.json, scoped to both tables (what the Salvage bench knows that is not gear: rocks, plants, ammunition, bait, deployables, repair kits, fertilizers, the capture crate; and the few vanilla items that carry a gear type without being gear: a spawner egg, a grenade, the developer items and every item of a creative or test quality), and the table's own trophy and kit by Custody.Input.Except here; both answer Refused:Protected. Then the station's metadata guard turns away any piece whose stack carries data no mod declared disposable (a bag with something in it), since this ritual consumes every piece it takes. Custody keeps ONE real stack (MaxQuantity 1) so wear and stamped stats travel into custody and back out intact if the ritual is interrupted; HeldOnly places only what the hand holds, never a match dug out of the backpack; Preview names the return as the piece lands. Every beat authors IsWork so the table stays lit between beats; every beat but the last is Paced and shrinks with Pace, and the ritual ends on the Payout's bloom, which holds its 1.5 seconds at any speed. Pace reads the native stat RPG_Disenchanting_Proficiency: untrained the ritual takes about 15 seconds (14.5), and the most the shipped gear reaches (the full kit, the grimoire in hand and the draught, 98 points) brings it to about 3, in even steps between. The kit pieces, the set tiers, the grimoire trophy and the draught all raise that stat, so a worker gets faster by wearing and drinking, never by anything this file needs to know about. A pack that wants a longer, slower ritual says so from its own extension instead of restating these beats: a Pace.Stretch lengthens every paced beat, a Pace.Clamp of its own raises the floor, and a ladder of its own can soften this one. Bonus rolls at the Payout beat (RollBonus), one pass per ritual, from four tables that each hold one concern: Disenchant_Essence (the ordinary Life essence, marked Expected so it lands on the plain output row), Disenchant_Void (the Void essence and Voidheart finds), DisenchantTrophy (the grimoire chase) and Disenchant_Kit (the four kit pieces). Retune any one by overriding that one small file. Every number here is balance data: beat lengths, pace floors, offsets, delays and clip lengths are all leaves.
Label: rpgstations.action.disenchant.label

Recipe.$Comment: Benches names the vanilla Salvage bench by its native bench id, and Types keeps the derivation to Processing recipes, which is the kind every salvage file is. No Yield: vanilla's own return is the point, and everything the table adds is a Bonus roll. Fallback.CraftingShare.Share 0.3 hands back a bit under a third of each exact-item line of the piece's own crafting recipe, per piece for a batch recipe, which stays under vanilla's own quarter-to-a-third salvage return; EssenceOnly then takes any gear piece with neither recipe, so a drop-only sword is unmade for its essence rather than refused. Input's Type list is the gear filter: add a Type here to put another class of item on the table, and protect any one item of it the table must not take in ProtectLists/Disenchanting_Tables.json.

Work.$Comment: Looping false makes the Steps program a ritual: one run per piece, then the session completes. MaxDurationMs is a safety cap far above any ritual's length.

Custody.$Comment: Input authors only Except, so acceptance stays what the recipe and the fallback derive (every piece the Salvage bench knows, plus every tagged weapon, armor piece, tool and utility piece) minus two holes of the table's own: its grimoire trophy, by id, and the disenchanter's kit, by the Disenchanter family tag the four kit pieces carry, so a find is never unmade by accident. The non-gear either route would otherwise admit (rocks, plants, ammunition, bait, deployables, the tagless repair kits, fertilizers and capture crate the Salvage bench knows, and the spawner egg, grenade and developer items that carry a gear type) is refused by ProtectLists/Disenchanting_Tables.json, one file scoped to both tables. Display sets the placed piece just above the crusher's mouth, six tenths of a block across, turning and bobbing the way a dropped item does; the Draw beat lifts it higher for its own length.

Pace.$Comment: The one factor is the native stat RPG_Disenchanting_Proficiency, read through hytale:stat. The highest reached floor's Scale multiplies every Paced beat (13 of the ritual's 14.5 seconds; the 1.5-second bloom holds), and the floors are spaced so each takes about 1.6 seconds off the whole ritual: 14.5, 12.8, 11.3, 9.6, 7.9, 6.3, 4.6 and 3.0 seconds. The four kit pieces carry 36 points between them, the kit's three set tiers add 28 (the last one only with the grimoire in hand), the grimoire trophy 14 in hand, the draught 20 for five minutes: the draught alone is about 11 seconds, the full kit about 8, the kit with the grimoire about 4.6, and all of it, 98 points, about 3. An extension's own Pace ladder multiplies into this one; this Clamp bounds the product, so author both sides here, and an extension's Clamp can only narrow it.

Steps.$Comment: Open, 0.8 seconds untrained and Paced: the double reaches over the piece while the table wakes into its Working look, then goes back to channelling once the gesture has played (ClipMs, which an animation's own speed sets, so it is not paced). The sigil rises from the placed piece itself (Target Display; RPG_Disenchant_Sigil authors a LifeSpan so it rides the prop) under the spellbook's page-turn charge.

Kindle, 3.2 seconds untrained and Paced: the double channels (no clip of its own: the Open gesture already handed it back to the channelling loop) while the power swells; two mote chimes land on delays that stretch with the beat. The sparks and motes (RPG_Disenchant_Kindle, the gem sparks in a green-gold copy with the eternal-seed motes) ride the placed piece itself (Target Display), so on either table they play on the piece being worked, not at the block; the system's own 7.5-second LifeSpan ends it on a long ritual, and on a shorter one the Draw beat's lift respawns the prop and takes anything still riding it with it, so the sparks never outlast this beat.

Draw, 4.8 seconds untrained and Paced: the double keeps channelling, the block deepens into its Drawing look, and the piece lifts and turns (the Display overlay). The overlay respawns the prop at the beat's entry, and a prop spawned this tick has been shown to nobody yet, so a cue aimed at it in the same tick would play at its position instead of riding it: the whole group holds 160 ms (Paced, so it shrinks with the beat, but any held cue waits for the next tick at least) and then the gather (RPG_Disenchant_Draw, its own LifeSpan) rides the lifted piece and the chime follows it. The channel aura goes on the worker's double at the same moment, for the rest of the session (no DurationMs: the double's effects come off at the session's end; on a worker with no double the effect's own Duration bounds it).

Surge, 3.6 seconds untrained and Paced: the double winds up, then goes back to channelling once the wind-up has played (ClipMs). The beam shell (RPG_Disenchant_Surge) and the signature sparks (a vanilla system with its own 0.6-second LifeSpan) ride the lifted piece; the layered charge builds under them, and the whole group holds 120 ms so the light shake lands after the pose change rather than on it.

Unmake, 0.6 seconds untrained and Paced: the release, after which the double goes back to channelling (ClipMs). Convert runs the matched row at entry, so the piece is consumed and its prop despawns in the same tick, and the block falls back from Drawing to Working. Target Display then resolves to where the lifted piece last stood, which is where the shatter plays: RPG_Disenchant_Flash folds the magic hit, the glass break and the crystal break into one bounded system so all of it lands there. The crystal break plays through RPG_SFX_Disenchant_Crystal_Break, a copy that bypasses the greater table's ducking, so the hum never swallows it.

Payout, 1.5 seconds fixed, the last beat and the only one no pace or stretch touches: RollBonus rolls the action's Bonus here, once per ritual, so the finds land while the bloom is up; each find's Cue moment holds about 450 ms (see Moments) so it arrives after the shatter has cleared. The bloom (RPG_Disenchant_Bloom, its own 2-second LifeSpan) plays where the piece stood and finishes on its own as the ritual ends; on the greater table the next piece's Open follows straight on.

Bonus.$Comment: One Lootable per concern, so a pack or a server owner re-tunes exactly one by shipping a same-id file. Every roll in them authors Trigger Cycle, the moment the Payout beat's RollBonus fires, and each find names one of the Cue: moments below.

Worker.$Comment: Seated the way the Sawmill seats its worker: Hold.Mount Surface Block mounts the hidden player on the table block's own seat (BlockType.Seats on the table's block item), which keeps them in place while the mouse turns the camera freely, and no Camera group is authored, so the camera stays the player's own. Getting up off the seat ends the ritual and hands the piece back. Animation.EmoteId is the channelling loop (RPG_Emote_Disenchant_Channel, a looping cast): the double starts in it, plays it through every beat with no clip of its own, and goes back to it after each beat gesture that names a Puppet.ClipMs, so it is always working. Puppet.Prop Source None keeps the double's hands empty for the whole ritual, whatever the worker is holding: the casting gestures need nothing in hand, and nothing in the worker's own hand is copied onto it. Author an ItemId prop here to give it something to hold.

Cue:Void_Find.$Comment: Void essence found: a violet impact and a small, capped portal flash at the piece's height, with the void eye's summon call through a copy that bypasses the greater table's ducking. The 450 ms hold lands it after the shatter.

Cue:Voidheart.$Comment: The rarest find: the epic drop glow and the block's top glow, both capped, a light shake, the portal opening and the void crawler's fade 300 ms behind it (again through a ducking-bypass copy).

Cue:Trophy.$Comment: The grimoire: gold with purple. The crown's rays sit two to three blocks up in their own system, so PositionOffset.Y -1 brings them down over the table; both systems are capped because neither ends on its own. The legendary-chest sting is a stereo file, so it reaches the worker in 2D through the effect's LocalSoundEventId rather than a positional sound.

Cue:Kit_Find.$Comment: A kit piece found (the cue Lootables/Disenchant_Kit.json's four rolls name): the uncommon drop glow, capped, and a coin chime, after the shatter. A Cue: id is author-defined; the engine's own Rare_Find id is never taken from an action's map, so a find that should sound like this table names this cue instead.

Completion.$Comment: The session's end, after the last piece (the greater table's queue drains before this plays).
